The extradition of Interpol Red Notice subject Oleksandr Zapichenko was secured in coordination with the Ministry of External Affairs, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the ED. Photo: Special arrangement
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) facilitated the extradition of a Ukrainian citizen from Romania to India on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). He was wanted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) for his alleged involvement in defrauding investors on the pretext of offering phenomenal returns.
The extradition of Interpol Red Notice subject Oleksandr Zapichenko was secured in coordination with the Ministry of External Affairs, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the ED.
“The subject was wanted in connection with a case registered by the Enforcement Directorate under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The subject, along with other accused persons, allegedly defrauded investors by inducing them to invest money on the false promise of exorbitant returns ranging from 6% to 11% per week,” the agency said.
The money-laundering investigation pertains to Platinum Hern Private Limited, which operated under the brand name ‘Torres Jewellery’ and allegedly lured several small and gullible investors into a fraudulent investment scheme by promising exceptionally high returns and referral bonuses. Low-value jewellery items were sold at grossly inflated prices, the ED said.
Alpesh Pravinchandra Khara, who allegedly acted on the instructions of Zapichenko, was arrested by the ED on March 26, 2025. The ED has quantified the proceeds of crime in the case so far at ₹177.12 crore. The agency filed a prosecution complaint on May 22, 2025.
Based on the ED’s request, a non-bailable warrant was issued against the Ukrainian national by a special Mumbai court on November 3, 2025. He was provisionally arrested in Romania on May 23, 2026.
The investigation revealed that the company concerned was operating a multi-level marketing-based Ponzi scheme and had collected huge amounts of money in cash from investors without obtaining the requisite approval from the Reserve Bank of India.
The funds collected from investors were laundered through various ‘hawala’ channels and subsequently used to purchase USDT cryptocurrency.
The accused was directly involved in converting cash deposits collected from investors into cryptocurrency. His alleged role in facilitating and arranging large-scale cash transactions further established his central role in the alleged money-laundering network.
At the ED’s request, an Interpol Red Notice was published against him. He was subsequently traced to Romania and arrested by the local authorities following an extradition request from India. “Following due legal process, the Romanian authorities granted the extradition of the subject to India,” the CBI said. The accused was handed over to an ED escort team in Romania and arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday.(November 17)
Since 2019, the CBI has coordinated the return of more than 280 accused persons wanted by various Indian enforcement agencies.
